sections.brief: How the Christian canon formed: Muratorian fragment, Athanasius's 39th Festal Letter (367, no burning order), Rome 382 (disputed Decretum Gelasianum), Hippo 393, Carthage 397/419, the East's slower closure, Florence 1442, Trent 8 April 1546 (24-15-16), Luther 1534, Westminster 1646 and the Protestant 66, the Ethiopian 81; Nicaea corrected (250-318 attended, 200-220 names on signatory lists, two bishops refused; it decided Arianism, Easter, Melitians, canons, not the Bible); Nag Hammadi 1945 and the Index 1559-1966 without suppression overreach. Figures: time (canon milestones); compare (claim vs record)

The Vatican Apostolic Archive: Paul V c.1610-12, 'secretum' = private, renamed by motu proprio of 22 October 2019; 85 km, 600+ fonds, 8th-20th centuries; access rules and opening by pontificates (1881, Pius XI 2006, Pius XII 2020, limit October 1958 as of 2025-26); documented holdings; the Library (80,000 manuscripts, 1.6m volumes). Figures: compare (claim vs record); stats

The Pius XII files opened 2 March 2020: what was opened; Wolf 2020 (Dell'Acqua memo, US inquiry of Sept 1942); Kertzer 2022 and reviews (Evans, Cucchiara) with the Osservatore Romano reply (Napolitano); Coco's König-Leiber letter of 14 December 1942 (published 2023); the Holy See's 'Ebrei' series online 2022-23 and Ickx's reading; what is and is not settled. Figures: time
